speaker_role: test-prep/consultancy marketer (self-described financial aid/college business channel, 'Cash for College')
commercial_incentive: Promotes a free downloadable guide ('the business of college') and frames college broadly as 'a business,' positioning the speaker as an expert resource
key_insights: States roughly 400 US universities require the CSS Profile, mostly private/elite schools, with a handful of selective public exceptions (examples cited: Michigan, North Carolina)
CSS Profile examines primary residence/real estate, retirement accounts, cash-value life insurance, annuities, and valuables/collectibles as part of assessing ability to pay
Notes the CSS Profile is used for both US citizens and international students applying to US colleges, a distinguishing feature versus FAFSA
States families should complete the CSS Profile annually, starting the October 1 window each year aid is needed, not just once
Describes CSS Profile fees: about $25 for the first school and about $16 for each additional school sent, with fee waivers available for qualifying students/families
specific_numbers_or_facts: About 400 US universities require the CSS Profile (per speaker), mostly private schools
CSS Profile filing opens October 1 (per video)
CSS Profile fee: about $25 for the first school sent, about $16 for each additional school
notable_or_distinctive: Provides a specific ballpark figure (~400 schools) for how many US universities actually require the CSS Profile, a scope detail often left vague in other CSS Profile explainer videos in this batch.
reliability_notes: Short promotional video with a 'college is a business' marketing framing; specific figures (400 schools, $25/$16 fees) are stated without citation and should be verified against current College Board figures, as fees and school requirements change over time.
